message:
Pin the toolchain, centralize dependencies, harden CI (#1)

- `rust-toolchain.toml` pins Rust 1.99 with rustfmt, clippy, and the
wasm32 target; it is the only place the version is set.
- Every dependency is declared in `[workspace.dependencies]`; crates use
`workspace = true`. Dropped the unused `thiserror`. `Cargo.lock` is
unchanged.
- Workflows use `actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain`, pin every
action by commit SHA (Node 24 versions), and default to a read-only
token; only the sync and deploy jobs get write access. Dropped
`configure-pages`, which was unused.

---------

Fix contributor lists

- Leave AI attribution keys (ai-model, ai-provider) out of top and
  active contributors; they carry shared diff metrics for the AI views.
- Show ten rows of new contributors and scroll the rest.

Do not mention accounts in the discovery report (#12)

GitHub emails every account mentioned in a pull request description, and
the discovery report linked contributors with a leading at sign.
Accounts are now plain links to their GitHub profiles, and profile text
that may contain handles (profile companies, unknown organizations,
alias values) is quoted in code spans, where GitHub does not create
mentions. A test fails if the report has an at sign outside a code span.
The Copilot review comment still mentions Copilot on purpose.

Sort company and affiliation configs, date current affiliations (#8)

Match bot names by word and post the Copilot comment once (#9)

Bot detection matched "bot" anywhere in a login, name, or email, so
people like Parag Ekbote were flagged and new contributors with such
names were classified as bots. Logins and email local parts now need a
word ending in "bot", and display names need the word "bot" or "robot".
dyu-bot is Derek Yu's personal account, so it gets a HUMAN identity
rule.

The discovery script posted the @Copilot comment on every update of the
pull request. Without COPILOT_TOKEN Copilot ignores it, so it is now
posted once, when the pull request is opened.

Add grouped Dependabot updates and JS linting (#2)

- Dependabot opens one grouped weekly PR each for Rust (cargo), JS
(npm), and GitHub Actions, with a 7-day cooldown before proposing a new
release.
- Adds a `package.json` with ESLint and Prettier for the web views (no
runtime JS dependencies); CI runs `npm run lint` and `npm run
format:check` instead of `node --check`.
- The deploy workflow reads the wasm-bindgen CLI version from
`Cargo.lock`, so Dependabot bumps of the exact-pinned crate keep the CLI
in sync.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

Discover companies and affiliation changes (#6)

- After each sync, `pulse discover --apply` proposes new companies,
`@org` aliases, email domains, affiliations, affiliation changes, and
earlier affiliations, and `scripts/discovery-pr.sh` opens or updates a
`bot/company-discovery` PR with the evidence. Ambiguous cases are listed
for review; `config/discovery.yaml` lists values never to propose.
- Signals: profile companies (now refreshed weekly, kept as
first/last-seen runs so changes are dated), public organization
memberships, and corporate commit email domains from Git (domain only,
never the address). `pulse sync --full-git` backfills domains for
existing history.
- The discovery PR gets CI dispatched for the required checks and an
`@Copilot` comment asking it to verify companies, accounts, and evidence
(uses a `PULSE_COPILOT_TOKEN` secret when set).
- New contributors whose login, name, or commit email contains "bot" are
classified as bots unless they have a curated affiliation; existing ones
are listed for review. Adds a `snyk-bot` BOT rule.

Report sync results on the workflow summary page (#5)

- `pulse sync --summary-file` appends a Markdown report: per repository
(git mode, new and newly merged PRs, new commits, relinked PRs, new
contributors, API points, time), API quota, failed or skipped
repositories, and state totals.
- `pulse summary` reports the built snapshot: size, activity over the
last 7/30/365 days, the most active repositories this week, and totals,
using the same queries as the site.
- The sync workflow writes both to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`;
push-triggered runs include the site data section.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

Add pull request review metrics (#17)

Collects submitted reviews with each pull request (same GraphQL query,
paged follow-up for PRs with more than 50 reviews) and stores them in a
new pull_request_reviews table. The first sync after merge rereads each
repository's PR history once to backfill reviews without a new clone;
locally that took about 19 minutes and 179 points. During that rescan
only PRs an incremental scan would have read are relinked, and PR pages
drop to 50 after a slow response.

The site adds review coverage (merged PRs reviewed by someone other than
the author before merge), median time to first review, top reviewers,
and review counts on repository, contributor, and company pages.
Self-reviews, bots, and AI accounts are not counted. The snapshot format
version is bumped.
